title: POSTCARDS FROM THE OTHER TOWN · VI
venue: Arthur's site · a romance the strip never ran · eight cards · Box 19
logline: His: the front is a bus's side mirror filling the card with the road going backward in it and a lighthouse in the mirror the size of a stamp; the back, one word.

panels.composition: The postcard's front: a bus's side mirror filling the card with a coastal road receding in it and a lighthouse in the glass no bigger than a stamp.

image.prompt: two-color coastal weekly illustration, a bus side mirror filling a card with a coastal road receding in it and a lighthouse the size of a postage stamp in the glass, no words legible

panels.name: Front

panels.composition: The postcard's back: the message side with the sixth word legible and the stamp placed crooked.

image.prompt: the back of a postcard drawn in ink, a divided back with an address side and a message side, the handwriting rendered as strokes with one word left legible, a small stamp with a tiny numeral in its corner, a crooked stamp, no words legible but one
image.notes: 'Wish you were here. It's far.' (canon: dw_2008-10-01, Gully's card). The strangers arrive at the canon's sentence by the sixth card. The one legible word: far. Stamp numeral: V.

panels.name: Back

art.line: razor-sharp brush and ink for the fronts; the backs in a stranger's hand, drawn as shapes but for one word each
art.palette: the fronts in the coastal weekly's two-color; the stamps in one color each
